purpose: Propafenone is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats, such as atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, and other abnormal heart rhythms. It helps your heart beat in a more regular, steady pattern. Your doctor prescribes it to lower your risk of serious heart rhythm problems.
how_it_works: Your heart beats because of electrical signals that travel through it. Propafenone works by slowing down those electrical signals so they move in a more controlled and organized way. Think of it like a traffic controller helping cars move smoothly instead of chaotically — it keeps the heartbeat steady and normal.
common_side_effects: You might notice a strange or metallic taste in your mouth, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, constipation, or blurred vision. Some people feel unusually tired or have headaches. These effects are often mild and may improve as your body gets used to the medicine.
warnings: This medication can sometimes cause new or worsened heart rhythm problems, so never stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, heart failure, or liver problems, as this drug may not be safe for you. Avoid grapefruit juice, and let all your healthcare providers know you are taking this medicine since it can interact with many other drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 150 mg taken by mouth three times a day, every 8 hours. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose to 225 mg or 300 mg three times a day based on how your body responds. The extended-release capsule (Rythmol SR) is typically taken twice a day. Always follow exactly what your doctor prescribes.
